propositions: Agent-authored mutation scripts executed without OS sandboxing can perform destructive filesystem operations (rm -rf) outside the worktree, as evidenced by the 2026-08-26 incident.

The rebar-debug and rebar-implement skills instruct agents to perform defect-seeded mutation as part of TDD workflow, but neither skill requires an OS sandbox for these code perturbation and test execution steps.

Both TDD skills must mandate mutation test execution inside an OS sandbox that denies writes outside the worktree and scratch directory, with complete inline invocations for macOS (sandbox-exec) and Linux (bwrap), capability probes, and a no-sandbox fallback strategy.
When a sandbox is unavailable, the mutation step must not execute deletion code against the real filesystem but instead assert on an injected seam to avoid hostile code execution risk.
The sandbox requirement must be carried inline within each skill with full, self-contained platform-specific commands rather than external references, and must be verified by regression testing.
